comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Phase 1 EXIT — root cause confirmed, mechanism and legitimacy both proven

### Root cause (a changeable artifact)

The mcp image never contains git metadata, so no attested gate can resolve a ref:

- `.dockerignore:5` excludes `.git`.
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:42` is `COPY . /app`, with `WORKDIR /app` at `:33`.

So `/app` is a plain source copy. `_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:293` raises
`cannot resolve ref 'origin/main' to a commit in '.'` because there is no repository to
resolve against.

### Runtime proof (dynamic claim, observed executing — not read from source)

    docker exec compose-mcp-1 sh -c 'ls -d /app/.git; cat /app/.deployed_ref; echo $REBAR_ROOT; pwd'
      ls: cannot access '/app/.git': No such file or directory
      d4a0a2a44 (feat/gerrit-ci-verified-gate)
      REBAR_ROOT=[<unset>]
      /app

`.deployed_ref` is a TEXT MARKER standing in for a clone. `REBAR_ROOT` is unset, so the repo
root resolves to the working directory `/app`, which has no `.git`. That is the whole
mechanism: every attested-source gate (`review_plan`, `verify_completion`, `review_code`,
`reconcile`) fails identically, and `attach_commits` can resolve no SHA.

**Discriminating detail:** `source: "local"` DOES run — which rules out "the gates are broken"
and isolates the fault to the attested-source path specifically, i.e. to the missing repo
rather than to the gate code. But a local verdict is never signed, so it cannot satisfy a gate.

### Legitimacy: incomplete-implementation (NOT feature-request)

Cited design authority — **ADR 0104 §3**:

> For the two op-cert kinds minted via MCP (plan-review at claim, completion-verifier at close
> — ADR 0049) to be **enforceable**, the MCP server signs them under the box's **EXISTING**
> opcert signing environment...

The capability was designed and approved with an operator ruling (2026-08-24, Option A). It was
never wired: the service shipped without a repo for the attested source to resolve against.
That is a defect-class miss, not a feature request.

### Net effect

No attestation can be earned through the live MCP server, so no task/story/epic can be closed
through it without a force — which agents are forbidden to use. The MCP surface is therefore
unable to complete the very workflow AGENTS.md directs agents to route through it.

### Attribution — by SCOPE OF WORK, not by introducing commit

No commit broke this; the service never had a repo, so `git blame` has nothing to find. The
scope-of-work owner is **`fd4a-4e91-f179-4932`** (`cibophobic-holohedral-esok`,
"rebar-mcp HTTP transport service on the AWS box"), the story that shipped the service and
its Dockerfile. A reviewer of that story could plausibly have caught that a container with no
`.git` cannot serve certified ops the ADR says it must — which is the test for a correct
attribution target. Recorded here because the `caused_by` link form is gated on the target
having a referencing commit and this is an omission.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Phase 2 — fix pushed as Gerrit change 2271

**Fix.** The entrypoint provisions a code checkout at `MCP_CODE_DIR` (default
`/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`) with `--filter=blob:none --single-branch --branch main`, and
`REBAR_ROOT` points at it. Blobless because the gates fetch objects on demand and a full clone
of this repo is prohibitively large. Backgrounded like the tickets clone so it cannot block
`exec` past the 120s readiness deadline; until it converges the gates fail exactly as they do
today, no worse. Presence requires a RESOLVABLE HEAD, not just `.git`, so a container killed
mid-clone re-clones instead of being mistaken for converged — the lesson from
`fathomable-yester-thrip`. `REBAR_ROOT`/`MCP_CODE_DIR` are set in BOTH docker-compose.yml and
`mcp_run_new`, which the compose-parity test pins.

**Test — held out, GREEN, and has teeth.**
`test_the_code_root_is_provisioned_so_attested_gates_can_resolve_main` was written and confirmed
RED (zero code clones executed; liveness anchor passing) BEFORE the fix, then moved out of the
implementing agent's worktree entirely — it was never visible to the fixer. Re-applied after:
GREEN. Defect-seeded mutation (remove the `provision_code` call, i.e. re-introduce the exact
root cause) returns it to RED with the git-call list showing no clone. It asserts observable
behaviour — what the script EXECUTED — not the presence of a line, so it is not a
change-detector.

**Scope & safety.** No existing test modified (the only test delta is the oracle). No new
dependency; no `src/` or manifest change at all. The `rm -rf` guard was generalised rather than
duplicated — both layers (absolute-non-`/` case guard, cd-relative glob) now live in the single
`clear_dir` every caller uses, and it gained trailing-slash normalisation so the globs cannot
degenerate. The existing unsafe-dir tests still exercise it unmodified and pass. Lint,
typecheck, shellcheck clean; 50 tests in the affected files pass.

**Step 7 parity sweep — the MCP server was the ONLY affected surface.** Both sibling containers
run attested gates and both were checked, not assumed:
- **review-bot — N/A.** `gerrit_client.clone_change_ref` builds its own working tree per review
  (`git init` + fetch of the change ref). It never relies on `/app`, and it demonstrably works.
- **opcert_service — N/A.** `opcert_service/workspace.py` provisions an ephemeral clone per job
  as a stated SECURITY property: "the worker fetches authoritative state ITSELF — never trusts
  the client... so review_plan / verify_completion read state the client cannot influence."

Both provision their own repository; the MCP server did not. That is the parity signature, and
it is why this is a single-surface omission rather than a class.

**Step 6 replication — NOT yet done, stated rather than implied.** The original report can only
be replicated against a DEPLOYED server, and 2271 has not merged or deployed. AC1-AC3 (a
`review_plan` through the live endpoint returning a verdict and persisting a certified
attestation) remain unverified until it lands. They are not ticked.

**Residual risk.** A failed code clone degrades to today's behaviour — the gates error — because
enforcement is out of scope by operator ruling. Accepted deliberately: gating promotion on a
backgrounded clone is what produced the rollback loop in `unfit-beneficial-whimbrel`.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Change 2271 got LLM-Review -1, and the blocking finding is CORRECT

Recording this against the fix rather than quietly amending, because the reviewer caught a
defect I introduced while fixing the original one.

**The finding.** `provision_code` was placed INSIDE the `if [ -n "\${MCP_TICKETS_PAT:-}" ]`
guard, but `REBAR_ROOT` is exported UNCONDITIONALLY in all three declaration sites
(Dockerfile.mcp ENV, docker-compose.yml, autodeploy.sh `mcp_run_new`). docker-compose.yml
documents a blank PAT as a SUPPORTED state — "BLANK IS FINE, the container still boots". So on
a blank-PAT deployment my change pointed the single global repo-root override at a directory
that is never created. That is a NEW failure mode introduced by the fix, not the one it removes.

**Why it happened.** I attached the code clone to the tickets credential because both use
`MCP_TICKETS_URL`, and treated one URL as implying one guard. The two clones have genuinely
different credential needs: the TICKETS clone pushes and needs the PAT; the CODE clone is
read-only against a repository that answers anonymously —
`GET https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack` returns **HTTP 200**,
which I have now verified rather than assumed. So the code clone needs no credential at all and
must not share the guard.

**RED first, again.** `test_the_code_root_is_provisioned_even_without_a_tickets_pat` is written
and confirmed RED for the right reason — with `pat=None` the recorded git-call list is `[]`,
zero clones, while the liveness anchor still passes, so the script demonstrably ran and skipped
the work. It is held out of the fixing tree exactly as the first oracle was.

**One existing test legitimately changes**, and it should be visible rather than buried:
`test_no_pat_skips_the_clone_but_still_converges_the_store` asserts `not run.cloned`, and
`Run.cloned` matches ANY clone. It was written when the tickets clone was the only clone. After
the fix a code clone DOES fire with no PAT, so the assertion is being narrowed to the tickets
clone specifically (`--branch tickets`), with `tickets_cloned`/`code_cloned` replacing the
ambiguous `cloned`. That is a deliberate behaviour change being reflected in the test, not a
test bent to pass — flagging it so it gets scrutiny rather than a nod.

The seven advisory findings are all real test gaps in the same change (blank-PAT path,
code-clone failure posture, the mount-absent skip branch, the idempotent short-circuit) and are
being closed in the same patchset.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Answering the REBAR_ROOT blast-radius advisory (rather than letting it pass as non-blocking)

The reviewer's advisory is ACCURATE and worth an explicit answer, because `REBAR_ROOT` is a
single global override and I am now setting it on a production container. Its consumers, read
off main:

- `src/rebar/config.py:310` — config DISCOVERY (where `rebar.toml` is found)
- `src/rebar/config.py:531` — `reconciler_repo_root`
- `src/rebar/_config_resolvers.py:240` — general `repo_root`
- `src/rebar/_config_resolvers.py:387` — `resolve_run_root`, the workflow-run scratch base

**The one that could have been serious is the ticket store, and it is safe — verified, not
assumed.** If the tracker path derived from `repo_root`, pointing `REBAR_ROOT` at the code clone
would have silently MOVED the tickets store and re-created the empty-tracker outage this whole
epic exists to fix. It does not: `config.tracker_dir()` reads `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` FIRST and
returns it verbatim before any `repo_root` call is reached (`config.py:138-156`), and compose
sets that variable explicitly to `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`. So the store is unaffected by
construction, not by luck.

**Config discovery does change**, and this is the honest residual: `rebar.toml` will now be read
from the clone rather than from `/app`. Both are the same repository, so they agree at boot —
but the clone is taken at container-start time and the image is built at deploy time, so a
container that starts appreciably later than its build could read a slightly newer `rebar.toml`
than the code it is running. In practice the two are minutes apart and `rebar.toml` changes
rarely; the alternative — leaving `REBAR_ROOT` unset — leaves EVERY attested gate unusable,
which is strictly worse. Recording it so the tradeoff is visible rather than discovered later.

The remaining consumers (`reconciler_repo_root`, `resolve_run_root`) are strictly IMPROVED by
the change: today they resolve against `/app`, which has no object DB at all, so anything
depending on them is already broken on this container.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## CORRECTION: change 2271 was NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT. This ticket is not fixed.

I wrote that 2271 fixes the attested gates, pending only deployment. It is deployed, and they
still fail. Correcting that here rather than letting the earlier comment stand.

### What 2271 did achieve — verified on the live container

    REBAR_ROOT=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code
    MCP_CODE_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code
    git -C /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code rev-parse origin/main
      -> 269f7b49c44fd87da2bf26f8f5d35ba6d9df6ad0
    git -C /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code rev-parse main   -> same
    origin -> https://github.com/navapbc/rebar.git [blob:none]

The repository is provisioned, healthy, and resolves BOTH refs. That half of the diagnosis was
right and the fix works.

### The remaining cause: the snapshot layer never consults REBAR_ROOT

`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:264` (and identically at `:503` and `:699`):

    root = str(repo_root) if repo_root else "."

When `repo_root` is `None` it falls back to the literal `"."` — the PROCESS CWD, which is
`/app` in the container, and `/app` has no object DB because `.dockerignore` excludes `.git`.
It never asks the config layer.

And none of the MCP LLM tools pass a `repo_root`: `_mcp_llm.py:116` (`review_code`), `:146`
(`scan_spec`), `:196` (`verify_completion`) all call `rebar.llm.*` without one. So every
attested-source tool takes the `None` -> `"."` path.

Demonstrated directly, from a non-repo cwd with REBAR_ROOT set:

    repo_root_or_none()  -> /Users/joeoakhart/71e7-codex-mcp-pat   (honours it correctly)
    snapshot default     -> "."                                    (ignores it)

### The experiment that settles it — and refutes the reported cause

A parallel Copilot session retried `review_plan` with an EXPLICIT full SHA and got the same
error: `cannot resolve ref '269f7b49c44fd87da2bf26f8f5d35ba6d9df6ad0' to a commit in '.'`. It
concluded the server's clone is 'stale, disconnected, or configured differently'.

That conclusion is WRONG, and the SHA is what disproves it: it is exactly the commit I verified
`/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code` resolves. A stale clone cannot explain failing to find a commit the
clone demonstrably contains. Looking in the WRONG DIRECTORY explains it exactly — and the error
message names that directory, `'.'`, not `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`. The `'.'` was the tell all
along.

### Class

Same family as `damageable-huge-xiphosuran`: shipped code bypassing rebar's own configured
resolver and substituting a hardcoded default. That one is `tracker_dir`; this is `repo_root`.

This ticket stays IN PROGRESS. AC1-AC3 remain unticked, correctly.

comments.body:
## Fix authored — the snapshot layer now honours the CONFIGURED repo root

**RED first, reproducing the production error byte-for-byte.**
`tests/unit/test_snapshot_honours_configured_repo_root.py` builds a real one-commit repo, points
`REBAR_ROOT` at it, `chdir`s to a directory that is NOT a repo, and calls
`resolve_ref("main", fetch=False)` with no explicit root — the exact shape of the deployed
container (cwd `/app` with no object DB, `REBAR_ROOT=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`). It failed with:

    SnapshotRefError: cannot resolve ref 'main' to a commit in '.'

which is the SAME message, naming the same `'.'`, that the live server produced. That is a
faithful reproduction rather than an approximation of one.

**The fix.** A single `_resolved_root()` seam in `_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py` replaces the three
`str(repo_root) if repo_root else "."` fallbacks (in `resolve_ref`, `materialize`, and
`materialize_tickets`). An explicit `repo_root` still WINS; only the `None` case changes, falling
back to `repo_root_or_none()` (`REBAR_ROOT`, then the git toplevel of cwd) before `"."`.

**A negative control guards the dangerous direction.**
`test_an_explicit_repo_root_still_wins_over_the_environment` asserts that `REBAR_ROOT` does NOT
override an explicitly-passed root. Getting that backwards would be a worse bug than the one
being fixed — silently reading a DIFFERENT tree than the caller named — so it is pinned rather
than left to reviewer attention.

**Mutation-checked.** Reverting `_resolved_root` to return `"."` turns the reproduction RED again
with the identical error and leaves the negative control passing. `make lint` clean,
`make typecheck` clean across 677 files.

**Why a seam rather than three edits.** The three call sites had drifted into the same hardcoded
default independently; a shared helper means the next snapshot entry point cannot reintroduce it
by copy-paste, and the reasoning (with the outage that motivated it) lives in one docstring.

**NOT YET DONE — the live-validation criterion.** This is authored and verified locally only. The
new mandatory AC requires `review_plan`/`scan_spec` to be OBSERVED returning a verdict through
`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp` after this lands and the container redeploys. That is
precisely the step I skipped when I claimed 2271 had fixed this ticket, so it is not being
skipped again: the box stays unticked until a live call is made and its response recorded here.

comments.body:
## Fix pushed as Gerrit 2275 — and I MOVED it mid-flight, which is worth explaining

**Where the fix landed, and why not where I first put it.** My first version added a helper to
`_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py`, replacing its three `str(repo_root) if repo_root else "."`
fallbacks. That was the deepest correct layer — and it would have FAILED CI.

That file sits at **exactly 800 LOC**, the locked hard cap. My version took it to **823**. Every
local gate passed: `make lint` clean, `make typecheck` clean across 677 files, 882 targeted tests
green. The module-size gate is a step in `_build-and-test.yml`, NOT a `make lint` target, so a
green local run is entirely consistent with a commit CI rejects. I only checked because a
parallel agent hit the identical trap on the same file an hour earlier and reported it.
`pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` is the local mirror; it is not in the default
selection.

The file had no headroom for even a one-line import, and I declined to delete a blank line to fit
— buying space with a cosmetic diff in a file at a hard limit is the exact pattern that had just
gone wrong.

**The relocation is better on the merits, not just a workaround.**
`llm/gate_source.resolve_gate_handle` is documented as the function that applies 'the configured
defaults for `None`', and it ALREADY does exactly that for `ref` and `source`:

    resolved_ref    = ref    or default_ref(repo_root)
    resolved_source = source or default_source(repo_root)
    repo_root       = snapshot_repo_root(repo_root)      # <- the third default it owed

The root was simply a default it forgot. It is also the single entry point every attested gate
passes through, so one change covers `review_plan`, `scan_spec`, `verify_completion` and
`review_code`. The helper itself lives beside `repo_root_or_none` in `_config_resolvers`, the
module that already owns root resolution — so the config layer resolves and the snapshot layer
consumes, rather than the snapshot layer reaching sideways into config.

**Evidence.** The original RED reproduced the production error byte-for-byte at the snapshot
layer (`cannot resolve ref 'main' to a commit in '.'`). After relocating I retargeted the test to
the layer actually changed and established teeth by mutation: replacing the new line with `pass`
returns it to RED, and the negative control (an explicit `repo_root` is never overridden by
`REBAR_ROOT`) stays green — that direction would be worse than the bug, since a gate would verify
a different tree than the caller named and still sign an attestation saying otherwise.

Gates: lint clean, typecheck clean (677 files), **module-size gate 4 passed**, 129 tests across
gate_source / plan-review / snapshot consumers.

**Residual, not fixed here:** `repo_snapshot.py`'s bare-cwd fallback remains for non-gate callers.
That is the same class as `damageable-huge-xiphosuran` and is left to it rather than forced into
a file with zero headroom.

**LIVE VALIDATION still unticked** — pending 2275 merging and the container redeploying.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Every **attested-source** LLM gate operation fails on the LIVE MCP server
(`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`, container `compose-mcp-1`, image
`compose-mcp:9499312eb7b05dc3d75d39c23ab74a5b4afc26b5`).

Observed 2026-08-27 against the live endpoint:

```
review_plan       {"ticket_id": "ruby-griffinish-goitered"}
  -> Error executing tool review_plan: cannot resolve ref 'origin/main' to a commit in '.'.
review_plan       {"ticket_id": "...", "ref": "HEAD"}
  -> Error executing tool review_plan: cannot resolve ref 'HEAD' to a commit in '.'.
verify_completion {"ticket_id": "..."}
  -> Error executing tool verify_completion: cannot resolve ref 'origin/main' to a commit in '.'.
review_plan       {"ticket_id": "...", "source": "local"}   -> RUNS (P1/P2/P3 emitted)
```

## Mechanism
The container's repo root has **no git metadata at all**. Verified in-container:

```
$ docker exec compose-mcp-1 sh -c 'pwd; ls -d /app/.git; git -C /app rev-parse origin/main'
/app
ls: cannot access '/app/.git': No such file or directory
fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
```

`docker inspect` confirms `WorkingDir=/app`, `Cmd=["rebar-mcp"]`, and the env carries
`REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets` but **no `REBAR_ROOT`** — so the repo root
resolves to the cwd `/app`, which is a plain source copy, not a work tree. The image ships
`/app/.deployed_ref` (`d4a0a2a44 (feat/gerrit-ci-verified-gate)`) as a text marker instead of a
real clone. `source=attested` pins a snapshot at `ref` against that root's object DB, so ref
resolution fails before any LLM call.

The tracker itself is unaffected: it is an out-of-tree clone reached via `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR`,
so all non-git tools (create/show/search/list/comment/edit/link/claim/transition) work.

## Impact
`attested` is the DEFAULT source for both gate ops, and a `local`-source verdict is never
signed. So **no plan-review or completion attestation can be earned through the live MCP
server**, and consequently no `task`/`story`/`epic` can be closed through it while
`verify.require_plan_review_for_close` is on — the only remaining path is `--force`, which
agents are prohibited from using. Reproduced live: probe task `ruby-griffinish-goitered`
(`c67b-ece5-707e-460e`) is stuck `in_progress` with
`plan-review close gate: unsigned: no certified plan-review attestation`, and the prescribed
remedy (`review-plan`) is the very operation that cannot run.

## Reproduction
1. Call `review_plan` on any claimable ticket through the live MCP endpoint with default args.
2. Observe `cannot resolve ref 'origin/main' to a commit in '.'`.
3. Repeat with `source: "local"` and observe it runs.

## Fix

Provision a real repository for the gate ops to resolve against, and point the repo root at it.

**Why not the obvious alternatives.** Shipping `.git` in the image (removing the
`.dockerignore:5` exclusion) bloats every layer and pins a main that goes stale the moment the
image is built — the gates need a ref that tracks main, not a frozen one. Re-using the tickets
clone at `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` is tempting since `MCP_TICKETS_URL` is the SAME repository, but it
conflates the code root with the tracker: two different lifetimes, two different refspecs, and
a reader can no longer tell which one a failure came from.

**Shape.** `provision_store` gains a sibling that clones the CODE side into
`/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code` — `--filter=blob:none --single-branch --branch main`, so it is a
blobless clone that fetches objects on demand rather than materializing the history — and
`REBAR_ROOT` is set to it (compose env + `mcp_run_new`, which must stay in parity). That root
carries `rebar.toml`, so config resolution moves from the source copy at `/app` to a real
checkout, which is strictly better: the two agree today, and a real root is what the config
seam expects.

**Ordering.** Like the tickets clone this is backgrounded, so it cannot block `exec` past the
readiness deadline. Until it converges the gates fail exactly as they do today — no worse.

**Enforcement is OUT OF SCOPE** (operator ruling, 2026-08-27). This change makes the attested
gates work; it does NOT add a deploy-time check that refuses to promote a container whose code
root failed to resolve. A failed code clone therefore degrades to today's behaviour — the
gates error — rather than blocking the deploy. That is a deliberate boundary, not an oversight:
gating promotion on a backgrounded clone is what produced the rollback loop in
`unfit-beneficial-whimbrel`, and re-introducing it here would trade one outage shape for
another.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] AC1: `review_plan` with default arguments against the deployed MCP server returns a plan-review verdict (PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE) rather than a ref-resolution error.
- [x] AC2: `verify_completion` with default arguments likewise returns a completion verdict.
- [x] AC3: A PASS from AC1 persists a signed plan-review attestation.
      OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-28: `foreign_key` is ACCEPTED as sufficient; `certified` is
      NOT required. Observed: the AC1 run returned `attestation.signed: true`, so the
      attestation IS produced and persisted; `plan_review_status(b928-3ab6-5985-417b)`
      through the deployed server then returns `verdict: foreign_key` because that
      environment holds no op-cert public key and so cannot certify its own signature.
      The original wording demanded `certified`; that is waived here. The missing public
      key remains tracked separately (`dire-expectable-terr…`, see Scope boundaries).
- [x] AC4: The deployed container exposes a git object DB for the repo root reachable by the gate ops (a real clone at the repo root, or an explicit `REBAR_ROOT` pointing at one), verified by `git -C <root> rev-parse origin/main` succeeding inside the container.

## Definition of Done
- [x] DD1: AC1-AC3 demonstrated against a deployed MCP server.

## Scope boundaries (operator rulings, 2026-08-27)

- **Enforcement is out of scope.** No deploy-time refusal; see the Fix section.
- **A shared op-cert is acceptable.** The server signing under the box's existing opcert
  environment (ADR 0104 §3, Option A) is the accepted design. The separate observation that
  the environment holds no public key, so `verify_signature` returns `foreign_key`, is tracked
  as `dire-expectable-terrapin` and is NOT in scope here.

- [x] **LIVE VALIDATION — REQUIRED TO CLOSE.** `review_plan` called through the deployed endpoint returns a VERDICT rather than `cannot resolve ref ... in '.'`, and an attestation is persisted.
      OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-28: `scan_spec` is DROPPED from this criterion, and a
      persisted-but-`foreign_key` attestation is accepted in place of a certified one.
      Evidence recorded in the LIVE VALIDATION comment on this ticket: `review_plan`
      and `verify_completion` both returned real verdicts (PASS) through
      `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp` against container
      `rebar-mcp-2dbdcc8abe2c-8093`, with `attestation.signed: true`.
      Evidence must be OBSERVED against the deployed server at
      `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp` and recorded in a ticket comment naming
      the tool(s) called, the arguments, and the actual response. A passing local test is
      NOT sufficient, and neither is a merged change: the container must have redeployed
      and served the call. This exists because a fix here was previously reported complete
      on the strength of a merge while the deployed behaviour was still broken.
